findings.rationale: Size-adjusted update norm is far above the federation (median norm ratio 3.73, z=+6.6; min norm ratio z=+3.6) while peers of similar size sit near 1.2-1.4. Mean cosine to the median update is low (0.27) and erratic per round: norm ratio 5.2 in round 1, cos ranging from -0.37 (round 17) to 0.78 (round 3). This pattern fits large random noise in uploads rather than a consistent sign flip or scaling. Local performance is normal (AUC 0.798, CITL 0.006), so the data itself looks fine and the anomaly is in the uploads.

Update norm is anomalous for its size (median norm ratio 3.729, z=+7.3; min norm ratio 2.81, z=+5.5) with a low mean cosine to the median update (0.216), so it looks like noise-dominated uploads. Local performance looks normal (AUC 0.8005, CITL -0.010), which points to the update channel rather than the labels. Per-round values were not pulled for OH, so the onset is inferred from the full-run summary.

Update norm is anomalous for its size (median norm ratio 2.727, z=+6.5; min norm ratio 1.616, z=+3.6) with a low mean cosine (0.212) and a negative minimum cosine (-0.188). This is the same noise-like signature as MN and OH. Local performance is close to normal (AUC 0.796, CITL -0.023). Confidence is lower because the evidence is only from the full-run screen, with no per-round confirmation.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views of client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income). Three clients (MN, OH, SC) show size-adjusted update norms about 2.7–3.7x their peers (z +6.5 to +7.3) with low cosine to the median update, while their local AUC and calibration look normal. The per-round values for MN show erratic cosine with a declining norm, which fits random noise in uploads (explanation_instability) better than a consistent sign-flip or scaling. I reported all three, with MN the most confident. Other leads were not confirmed: AR's AgeGroup 12 O/E outlier did not reproduce at a narrower query; AL's and NV's drift and NV's high ECE were spiky across rounds and too noisy to call. Attribution churn is elevated across rounds, which is consistent with the update anomalies but does not identify a client. The 20.0 budget is fully spent.
